VBO:0200757.summary: Watchful around strangers, Kars dogs traditionally protect livestock and the people tending them in northeastern Turkey. Their job is to stay with cattle, sheep or goats and deter predators and intruders, rather than move the stock. The named regional population was reported at a 1996 shepherd-dog symposium and has since been studied and bred at Kafkas University.
VBO:0200757.shortDescription: A watchful northeastern Turkish livestock guardian, working alongside cattle, sheep and goats to deter intruders.

sources.title: Determination of Kars Shepherd Dog Raised in Turkey
sources.evidence: Own field survey of52 adults aged2–8 across northeastern Turkish provinces records guarding cattle, sheep, goats, owners and property against predators and intruders; explicitly distinguishes this work from stock herding. Reported rectangular adult measurements support functional robust proportions, without exaggerated earlier ideal weights.

sources.title: Fertility and Growth Traits, Some Body Measurements, and Morphological Characteristics of Kars Shepherd Dogs
sources.evidence: Introduction identifies Kars as a regional genetic resource with similarities to Caucasian Shepherd, reports its1996 named presentation and2002 registration; Methods documents16 adult dogs aged3–8 at Kafkas University. This establishes the named contemporary study population, without transferring puppy growth, health or reproduction results.

sources.title: Kars Turk Coban Kopegi: official Turkish Patent registration40
sources.evidence: Named Kars Turkish Shepherd registration independently supports current identity. Morphology page describes broad bear-like head, natural hanging ears, substantial deep body and strong limbs, fluffy coat and full long-haired tail curving toward the back. Large ideal numerical sizes and administrative/breeding claims are excluded.

VBO:0201256.summary: Boisterous and outgoing, Tasmanian Smithfields can retain the independent approach of a farm worker. Breeder Matthew Larner describes dogs that start training later and work more naturally than more controllable herding dogs. Farmers have shaped this variable working type for moving cattle and sheep, while keeping it as a companion too.
VBO:0201256.shortDescription: An outgoing Tasmanian working type, shaped by farmers for cattle and sheep and described as a natural worker.

sources.title: How the Smithfield dog breed went from London meat markets to working dog in Tasmania
sources.evidence: Larner describes boisterous/outgoing dogs, an independent and natural working approach, later training, cattle/sheep work and variable farm-selected type also kept as a companion. He expressly reports some long tails and some natural bobtails. Current supplied adult working-dog photographs support rough shaggy coat and developed working anatomy. Historical British descriptions and an individual owner's suitability anecdotes are excluded.
